analysis: All three changed files are test fixtures. Each has one change: the stub LanguageModel.prepare signature moves from (input, cache, windowSize) to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters). This tracks an upstream mlx-swift-lm protocol change. The changed lines are EngineV2ResliceUnwindTests.swift:98, FlintContextAdmissionTests.swift:262 and CancelledPrefixTestSupport.swift:84. Each stub still returns .tokens(input.text), so no production code, key handling, attestation, encryption, prefix-cache storage, authorization or networking path is touched. The changed code lives in test targets and does not ship in the provider artifact. The surrounding tests cover failure-unwind ordering, context-admission limits and cancelled-prefix behavior. They are unchanged and only assert existing invariants, such as releasing weights before KV grant regrowth and rejecting over-context requests before engine admission. No threat-model asset, boundary or mitigation (T-041, TB-007, T-010, T-028) is weakened. One integration question remains: the production Sources diff is not in this batch, so it should confirm that the dependency or protocol bump behind the new prepare signature does not change prefill or state behavior in the SSD prefix cache or admission paths. That is outside the supplied evidence and is not a finding here.
